answer: Cross-epoch reputation carryover. Each identity accrues a behavioural history across epochs; a new identity starts at a neutral vertex with no history. The rule: an identity's score can only change by a bounded increment per epoch, so sudden high-value actions from an unknown identity are capped until it accumulates consistent history. An attacker wanting N effective identities must operate each one through many epochs to reach useful weight—a voyage of repeated participation—rather than minting fresh ones. A lotus of patience: the per-identity cost is sustained genuine activity over time,
